title: delegated-admin-approval-log-retention
content:
Status: quick PRD draft / design notes (not final)
Owner: Asha Patel (PM)
Context
- Problem: customers deploying Redwood Private want: strong audit logs + flexible retention policies + approval gates for high-risk actions (network changes, key rotation, model pinning). They also expect to run in their VPC/on-prem with customer-managed networking and want clear export/ingest patterns for SIEM/EDR.
- Goal: define a pragmatic feature set that provides delegated admin approval flows, tamper-evident audit events, configurable retention/export, and clear interaction points with customer-managed networking (VPC peering, dedicated routes, firewall rules).
- Non-goal: full-blown RBAC rewrite — we will rely on existing RBAC primitives and extend with approval gate hooks.
High-level requirements
1) Audit logs
   - Event coverage: admin actions (create/modify/delete resources), network config changes (VPC peering, IP allowlists), key material ops (KMS/HSM rotate/grant/revoke), deployment rollouts, model-version pins, login/auth events (token grants, API key use), approval gate events (request, approve, reject), system fallback events (auto-fallback to hosted variant).
   - Schema: JSON line events, each event MUST include: timestamp (ISO8601), event_id (uuid), actor (user id / service id), actor_role, action, resource_type, resource_id, prev_state (optional), new_state (optional), request_context (ip, request_id), outcome (success|failure|skipped), approval_id (optional), tenant_id, region, encryption_meta (kms_key_id if present).
   - Integrity: option for append-only signed log bundles. Provide two modes: 1) customer-managed S3 export with manifest + HMAC signing (lightweight), 2) write-ahead log with envelopes signed by platform KMS and optional customer-managed key (HSM) for on-prem installs.
   - Retention controls: per-tenant and per-event-type retention policy. UI + API to set retention window (30d, 90d, 1y, 7y, custom). Support legal-hold flag to override retention. Default for private customers: 365 days.
   - Exports: scheduled export to customer S3/MinIO/FTP or push to syslog/Elasticsearch/Datadog; support for NDJSON & CSV transforms. Exports must preserve original envelope and include signature metadata.
   - Search & retrieval: lightweight index for last 90d of events for console search. Older events available via export only.
2) Approval gates / delegated approvals
   - Use cases: high-risk network changes; KMS/HSM key rotation; granting administrative scopes; production model rollouts (pinning to specific weights).
   - Flow: request -> auto-scan -> delegate -> approval -> enactment -> audit event.
   - Roles: requester, approver, delegator, emergency-break-glass (EBG). Approver groups can be defined (min 2 approvers for critical ops). Support configurable SLO for auto-timeout and escalation.
   - UI/CLI/API: API to create approval_request with metadata (reason, TTL, affected_resources, proposed_changes, dry_run_output). Response includes approval_id and status. Console shows queue, filters, comments, and audit trail.
   - Delegation: tenant admin can delegate approval rights to specific identities (service accounts) with time-limited tokens. Delegation itself is auditable and requires approval if crossing risk thresholds.
   - Emergency override: EBG can force through, but does create a high-priority, immutable audit event and triggers mandatory post-mortem requirement stored in the audit log.
3) Interaction with customer-managed networking
   - Visibility: any change that touches networking constructs (route tables, firewall rules, gateway attachments, NAT configs) must be surfaced to the approval gate.
   - Enforcement model options for private installs: 1) Control-plane-enforced — Redwood control plane validates and rejects invalid requests before calling customer APIs; 2) Customer-proxy-enforced — control plane sends signed desired state to customer-side agent which applies changes under customer's network ACLs — agent reports back success/failure.
   - Connectivity modes supported: VPC peering, PrivateLink equivalents, IPsec tunnels, on-prem NAT traversal. Document necessary ports and egress rules for agent communication.
   - Config drift detection: periodic scan of customer network objects vs last approved state. Drift events generate audit events and optionally auto-open remediation approval requests.
4) Security & compliance
   - Encryption: audit exports encrypted at rest using customer KMS where available. Provide envelope encryption model: platform signs, customer encrypts.
   - Tamper evidence: support signed manifests and sequence numbers; provide verification tools (hash chain verification) that customers can run locally.
   - Certifications: design to support SOC2/ISO needs (retention proof, access logs, segregation of duties).
5) Operational concerns and SLOs
   - Latency: approval flow should support synchronous approvals for simple ops (<500ms for local approval evaluation) but human approvals are expected in minutes.
   - Storage estimate: rough calc — 2KB avg per audit event. For a mid-size tenant (10M tokens/day, 200 infra ops/day) estimate 600KB/day (ops) + generation events ~ 100MB/day; retention at 1y -> 36.5GB. Need to show calculator UI for customers.
   - Backfill & replay: support reingest of historical events for compliance audits.
Acceptance criteria (v1 minimal)
- Audit events cover admin/network/key lifecycle and approval events; delivered as NDJSON and exportable to S3.
- Console shows pending approvals queue and history; API parity exists for primary flows.
- Retention policy controls per tenant with default 365d; legal-hold can be toggled via API.
- Customer-managed network changes are gated and either enforced by control plane or agent mode available.
- Signed export bundles and verification tool available for beta customers.
Implementation sketch / milestones (tentative)
- M1 (4 weeks): event schema + internal writer + simple NDJSON export to S3, basic retention TTL enforcement, minimal console view of events.
- M2 (6 weeks): approval API + console queue + basic delegation model + two-approver policy.
- M3 (6 weeks): customer-side agent for proxy-enforcement (alpha), signed envelope model + verification CLI, export integrations (Syslog/Elasticsearch).
- M4 (6 weeks): drift detection, emergency override flow, legal-hold workflow, docs and runbook for SOC2.
Open questions / tradeoffs
- Signed logs: HSM-backed signing vs HMAC manifest for S3 — HSM adds complexity for on-prem installs. Need security input (Ravi).
- Retention storage burden vs cost sensitivity: should we offer tiered storage (hot 90d index, cold archival) and pass cost to customers?
- Approval UX: do we allow Slack/email approvals (easy) vs strict console-only (more auditable)? Slack approvals complicate identity mapping.
- Delegation: how granular should we get? per-resource vs per-action. Start coarse (action-level).
- Agent connectivity: for strict air-gapped installs, agent deployment model may be required — need infra engineering time estimate.
Risks
- Overcomplicating RBAC leading to long implementation timelines.
- Acceptance by customers if log export guarantees are weak.
- Network enforcement model may require per-customer engineering for legacy environments.
Notes / TODOs (short)

- Prototype NDJSON sample events and verification CLI (Jinsoo).
- Add example retention calculator to console mock (Lena).
